memberCategories.renderer: Owns or inherits an implementation that draws Mermaid diagrams; wrapping another project's renderer alone does not qualify.
memberCategories.parser: Provides Mermaid syntax analysis, validation, formatting or structured editing APIs.
memberCategories.editor: Provides interactive diagram authoring, including browser and IDE applications.
memberCategories.integration: Connects an existing engine to a host, runtime, document workflow or output representation.
memberCategories.plugin: Extends another engine's layout or rendering pipeline.
memberCategories.distribution: Repackages an existing implementation. A package may also have another responsibility.

method.classification: categories record observed responsibilities and may overlap; an omitted category is not a verified absence. relation describes verified ancestry; roles select benchmark populations. None substitutes for the others. A catalogued discovery hit matches an inventory identity, not an exhaustive responsibility review. Existing categories use the source evidence recorded with each member; they do not claim a fresh runtime audit or complete source review of every responsibility.

discovery.review: Retain every search hit and its query/source provenance before classification. sources[].repo records each observed repository URL before identity normalisation, or null for absent metadata; the candidate's convenience repo may instead use inventory fallback. The report merges repository/package identities, including unambiguous curated npm ownership when repository metadata is absent. Conflicting repository observations and ownership remain visible for review with matched members recorded. It marks known members and leaves new candidates for source review, without rewriting this inventory or changing benchmark populations.
discovery.limits: Default one page of 50 hits per query; --pages and --per-page expose the bounds. Search ranking and API indexing limit recall. Record truncation and failures; the result is not an exhaustive ecosystem census. GitHub discovery requires the authenticated gh CLI. Web/topic searches and release/readme links can supplement these sources.
discovery.historicalExclusions: rendererBenchmarkExclusions records why the 18 October renderer census excluded package groups. These are benchmark exclusions, not community membership decisions; unreviewed integrations remain discovery candidates. eval/fork-graph/population.json retains its dated renderer benchmark population.

Existing observations and renderer peer rankings retain their dates and scope.

peers named with repository links in docs/design/families/{c4,gantt}.md and docs/project/prepared-text-geometry-plan.md
npmQueries: verbatim parent descriptions, 3 pages each: "Render Mermaid diagrams as beautiful SVGs or ASCII art", "Ultra-fast, fully themeable, zero DOM dependencies", "Markdownish syntax for generating flowcharts", "Markdown-ish syntax for generating flowcharts, mindmaps"
method.followed: Provenance statements in candidate READMEs, UPSTREAM.md and THIRD_PARTY.md were followed one hop (grok-build, mermaidtext, opencode, simonw/tools).
method.keep: Discover Mermaid renderers, syntax tools, editors, integrations, plugins and distributions before deciding benchmark eligibility. Depending on another engine, lacking an npm package, low stars or separate Git ancestry does not exclude a community member. Source-check responsibility and dependencies before classification; record unreviewed hits as candidates.
method.lineage: A GitHub fork shares its parent's root commit. Default branches were fetched commit-only (git clone/fetch --filter=tree:0); git rev-list --max-parents=0 gives rootCommits. vsParent is git rev-list --left-right --count parentHead...head.
method.relations: Node relation: root = the language origin; fork = shares the parent's root; port = no shared root, and a README, NOTICE or UPSTREAM file says the code was derived; binding = packages another node's renderer for a new runtime; independent = no shared root and no derivation claim. Edges add depends-on, inspired-by and vendors (an otherwise independent implementation copies the target's grammar or spec files), each with its evidence path. unverified means no ancestry classification was established; membership and responsibility do not imply a shared or separate Git root.
method.facts: branch = the default branch (anomalyco/opencode: v2, where its renderer lives); head = git ls-remote of that branch; lastCommit = committer date of head; license = manifest field, else LICENSE text; release = highest plain vX.Y.Z git tag, peeled; packages = npm view <pkg> version gitHead license, with provenanceCommit from the npm SLSA attestation; publishedFromDefaultBranch = provenanceCommit or gitHead is an ancestor of head.
notPossible: Original 18 October snapshot: star counts were not refreshed and the GitHub API was not used. July 2026 star ranks are in eval/mindmap-gitgraph-content-corpus/fork-snapshot.json.
Original renderer lineage is commit evidence only. The 23 October discovery pass uses GitHub search, but does not infer lineage for new application members.
The original renderer census lists only snapshot forks and forks with their own npm package; the broader discovery pass has no such membership gate and retains its search bounds.
crates.io and the Go module proxy were not queried; Rust and Go versions are git tags and manifest fields.
outputs and runtime are as stated by each README, not executed.
method.roles: language-reference, ancestor, self, peer (browserless renderer worth comparing on speed, payload and output), terminal-peer, parser-peer, observed (catalogued but not selected for renderer benchmarks; application or integration comparisons may still apply).
method.outputs: svg, png, jpeg, pdf, ascii-unicode (includes ANSI-coloured text), ast, diagnostics, mermaid-text, react-flow, excalidraw.
method.benchmarkEligibility: Every node has an explicit per-node eligibility classification/reason and operation adapter enrollment. Configuration is not a measurement/pass. Unknown public APIs and absent adapters are unmeasured until actual attempts; no private-host or credential blockers are inferred. Validators/formatters/converters compare only applicable operations. Source/history aliases require identical complete Git pins plus admitted compiled/distributed bytes and identical reviewed build/runtime protocols; shared roots/ahead counts alone never authorize evidence reuse.
